flags.title: Compliance status of the supplied short links is unresolved
flags.detail: The short links are not claimed to be invalid. Associates Program Policies Participation Requirements (w) restrict a link-shortening service in a manner that makes it unclear that the link goes to an Amazon Site (S02). Whether the link.amazon short links fall within that restriction has not been determined. The site does not use the short links for outbound links; they appear only as source evidence. Added 2026-11-20: Amazon's Associates help (S13) states that Amazon full links and Amazon short links are supported in the OneLink setup, and that third-party shortened links are not. Participation Requirements 2(a) requires the Associates tag as a parameter in each Special Link (S02). None of the five observed product redirects contains a tag parameter; the count in this field said "four" until session 66f2548a corrected it on 2026-11-20, after PR #10 established that all five links resolve (see products and data/observations/2026-11-20-reverify-66f2548a.json, which enumerates every query parameter seen on each resolved URL). Attribution of the link.amazon links to shopnow047c-20 therefore remains unconfirmed, and this flag stays open. Sharpened 2026-11-20 with the verbatim policy text, now read in full rather than from an excerpt: Participation Requirements 6(w) reads "You will not use a link shortening service, button, hyperlink or other ad placement in a manner that makes it unclear that you are linking to an Amazon Site." That clause turns on whether the Amazon destination is unclear, and it does not ban shorteners as such - which is why this flag records the links as unresolved rather than as a violation. The clause they are observed to fail is 2(b): "you must include your Associates ID or 'tag' ... as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site." (S02)
flags.manual_step: Check the supplied short links against Associates Program Policies (w) and the Associates tracking reports. Decide whether to keep them as evidence only or to replace them completely.

flags.title: Program Policies bar using Special Links or Program Content to develop machine learning models without Amazon's prior written approval
flags.detail: Participation Requirements §5, read verbatim 2026-11-20: "You will not, without or express prior written approval, use, or allow any third party to use, any Special Links or Program Content to develop machine learning models or related technology." (S02) The brief for this project asks for an AI-powered platform that automates product research and generates content. That is not prohibited outright - the clause is about using Special Links or Program Content as model input - but it puts a hard boundary on the automation the brief describes, and no earlier session recorded it. Everything built so far stays inside it: no Amazon content was used to train or fine-tune anything, product facts were read from manufacturer and Amazon pages by a human-directed process and cited, and outbound links are constructed from an observed ASIN plus the tracking ID rather than harvested programmatically at scale.

Record the answer here. Do not build the automated product-research pipeline in the brief until that answer exists.

flags.title: The Site may not have price tracking or price alerting functionality unless Amazon agrees
flags.detail: Participation Requirements §6(y), read verbatim 2026-11-20: "Unless otherwise agreed by Amazon, your Site must not have price tracking and/or price alerting functionality." (S02) The brief asks the platform to "analyze pricing" and to track conversions. Recording prices for internal analysis is a different act from shipping a price-tracking feature to readers, and only the second is barred by 6(y) - but the distinction has to be deliberate, not accidental. Related and stricter: §2(b) allows the Site to show prices and availability only where Amazon serves the link or the data comes from the Creators API or PA API. Neither is in place, which is why the build gate fails on any currency amount in the HTML and why FLG-016 stands.
flags.manual_step: Decide explicitly: no price feature on the site (current, and the safe reading), or apply for PA API / Creators API access and get Amazon's agreement before building one. Any suggestion on the Suggestions page that would surface a price is marked as needing this decision first.

flags.title: The root site ships a click counter and no privacy notice
flags.detail: Participation Requirements §3(e) makes the Associate responsible for "disclosing on your Site accurately and adequately and otherwise satisfying applicable legal requirements, either through a privacy policy or otherwise, the use of cookies, pixels, and other technologies by you and third parties and how you collect, use, store, and disclose data collected from visitors" (S02). The root site loads assets/analytics.js on every page and posts outbound-click events to a configurable endpoint. The script is genuinely privacy-preserving - the gate asserts it sets no cookies, no localStorage and no sessionStorage - and the endpoint is empty by default so nothing is sent. But there is no page telling a reader any of that. The only privacy notice in the repository is legacy/arena-83a43a96/privacy.html, which belongs to a superseded site and is not linked from the current one.

flags.title: The tracking ID's shape does not match the example format in the policy, which is not the same as being wrong
flags.detail: Participation Requirements §2(b) gives the tag format as "XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate" (S02). The supplied ID `shopnow047c-20` has an eleven-character prefix, not five, and a two-digit suffix that does match. Because the clause expressly allows other designated formats, the shape proves nothing either way: it cannot confirm the ID is valid and it cannot show it is invalid. FLG-011 previously rested on an Associates help page (S03) that IDs end in -20, which is a weaker basis than the policy text and still only a format observation. Recorded so nobody later reads the eleven-character prefix as evidence of a problem. Separately, §1(g) bars any Amazon trademark or variant in a tag or Associates ID; `shopnow047c` contains none, which is a genuine pass.
flags.manual_step: Export the tracking-ID list from Associates Central and confirm `shopnow047c-20` appears on it. That closes FLG-011 and this flag together.

flags.title: Three copies of the same five products are crawlable, and robots.txt advertises two of them
flags.detail: The brief asks for one site to index. The repository publishes three surfaces covering the same five products: the root site at `/` (23 pages, tools/build.mjs), a second publication at `/editorial/` (tools/build.py), and the first session's preserved site at `/legacy/arena-83a43a96/` (11 URLs in its own sitemap). robots.txt declares two Sitemap lines - the root one and the editorial one - so crawlers are pointed at both publications deliberately. `/legacy/` is not declared but is not disallowed either, so it is crawlable and can be found through any link to it. Near-duplicate coverage of the same products across three paths splits whatever ranking signal the site earns and gives a crawler no reason to prefer one. All three also carry outbound links, so the same reader intent is served from three templates. Keeping the earlier sessions' work was the right call for provenance; serving all of it to a search engine is a separate decision that has not been made. Verified by reading robots.txt, sitemap.xml, editorial/sitemap.xml and legacy/arena-83a43a96/sitemap.xml.
